output.brief:
The rise in cancellations is not mainly a pricing problem. The data points to the Quillbook accounting connector. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March. Since then the connector has silently dropped or duplicated invoices. About 1,200 of the 1,900 Quillbook-connected accounts were affected, and 34% of those have cancelled, against 8% of those with no recorded failure. Quillbook accounts churn at about 6% a month whether or not they are on the price lock. Accounts with no connector show almost no change (1.8% to 1.9%), whatever their seat count or price. The "bigger increase, more churn" pattern arises because Quillbook accounts have more seats. The failures are logged as warnings, so the health panel never showed them.

What to do:
1. Make the Quillbook fix (move to the v3 interface, 3–4 weeks) the top engineering priority.
2. Contact all Quillbook accounts, including those who cancelled, to correct their invoices.
3. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold on. It has kept 3,870 duplicates out of customers' books.
4. Don't roll back the price, which would cost about $220k a month.
5. Hold the Tallymarsh rebuild until its log has been reviewed.

Confidence is fairly high. The Tallymarsh log is still unreviewed.
